audits.keepRateNote: 14 keeps of 20 contrast-shaped candidates exceeds the 20% advisory. Re-examined: 6 are condition-4 self-argument ('No. Again.', 'A fair guess. No.', 'No. Slower.', 'oh, Light, no', 'Nobody.' reasoning chain, 'Except she wasn't anywhere on her own any more'); the rest are binary diagnostics driving action (L79, L279, L355, L465), spatial precision (L59, L397), and one deletion-test failure carried by self-argument (L211). findings.text: They don't fan out. They close.

findings.text: Then a young stag with his antlers laid back, and another doe, more crashing in the holly behind them, and they weren't swerving.

findings.suggestedFix: Then a young stag with his antlers laid back, and another doe, more crashing in the holly behind them.

audits.secondSweep: Dedicated P5/P6 sweep re-read every sentence for inanimate/abstract subjects with agency, desire, cognition, combustion or physical-behavior verbs. Added A-INT-01 (Reaching told), A-INT-04 (Finding out wanted), A-INT-05 (Death left/came). Road/geography verbs (ran, went up, met, bent, gave out, came down to) are literal path-geometry idiom with no intent. Contamination/ward/line verbs (travels, seeping, pressed in, pulling, working at, sending) are the chapter's literal in-world mechanism (subject-matter defense). No permission tags found ('Let the elf hear it' and 'Let her count her costs' are imperatives about a person, outside the closed tag set). Body-part subjects that are involuntary (chin hit her chest, stomach rolled over, ears going hot, hand wouldn't close, hands stopping mid-gesture after 'before she meant to') kept under the P8 reflex exception.

findings.pattern: intent-smear-P5 (personified abstraction 'Death left... when it came')
findings.text: Death left its own mark when it came, flat and cold, laid over a body from the outside.
findings.subject: Death
findings.realAgent: the ordinary dying of a body, which carries a flat cold signature
findings.reason: Pattern 5. Death is personified as an arriving agent leaving a mark; the concrete thing is the signature an ordinarily dead body carries, which is what Jaina compares against the anatomy-slab carcasses.
